notes: 'leṣānanda abhayānandena likhitaṃ': 'leṣānanda' has no case ending. Most likely it is the first part of an uninflected compound naming two scribes (Lekhānanda and Abhayānanda), with ṣ written for kh as often in Newar manuscripts. It could also be a corruption, or a word meaning 'scribe' or a kinship term, so treat it as a second scribe only with low confidence. The catalogue gives 'Leṣānanda? Abhayānanda'. The colophon has no date or place. The colophon also gives the text title in several forms (Ratnāvadānamālā / Aśokāvadānamālā, Durgatipariśodhanadhāraṇīmaṇḍala chapter).
